threatAssessments.description: Anthropic's Claude Enterprise: an AI assistant delivered as a service and used across the company for drafting, analysis, research and coding help. Staff sign in through company single sign-on, and connectors give it read access to approved document sources. Approved for data up to Confidential. This is a sample with illustrative answers.

profile.ssoMethod: SAML 2.0 single sign-on, with SCIM provisioning from the identity provider

DP-03.action: Block uploads of files labelled Restricted at the secure web gateway.
DP-03.comment: Restricted files can be uploaded by mistake.

DP-11.action: Extend data loss prevention to browser prompts and uploads for AI assistants, starting in monitor mode.
DP-11.comment: The most likely way sensitive data leaves through this tool is a well-meaning user pasting it in.

DP-22.action: Set a workspace retention period that matches the records schedule.
DP-22.comment: Old conversations add to what would be exposed in a breach or a legal hold.

DP-25.action: Finish the privacy impact assessment and have the privacy office approve it before the company-wide launch.

VC-15.action: Accepted: the assistant isn't a system of record. Review if teams start keeping project knowledge only there.
VC-15.comment: Loss of the service would cost convenience, not records.

VC-07.action: Write an exit plan covering data export, deletion confirmation and a replacement tool.

VC-10.action: Check the contract's processing locations against the data residency standard and record the result.

VC-13.action: Closed by the same SIEM export as the central logging gap.

threatAssessments.summaryNotes: Sample assessment. Overall business impact is Moderate, driven by confidentiality: a privacy breach or loss of confidence if sensitive data were exposed through prompts, uploads or connectors. The vendor-side controls rely on its assurance reports. The gaps are on our side: audit logs aren't monitored centrally, data loss prevention doesn't cover prompts and uploads, retention isn't set, and there's no exit plan. Sending audit logs to the SIEM and extending data loss prevention bring the highest risks from Moderate to Low.
